lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Hiya Junior! Just getting the crumble stuff out. Do you know if we've got any oats left, or did I finish them off? Oh, and how was your day, are you knackered before the weekend shifts?
lines.do: Gets flour, butter, sugar and apples out onto the counter and looks in the cupboard for oats

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Hiya Hayley! Oats, hmm, I think there's a bit left at the back, behind the rice, I saw a bag the other day. Knackered yeah, feet are killing me, but tonight's my night so I'm not complaining. Had a mad one today, a bed got stuck in the lift, Colin swore it was me, it was not me! Anyway, how's your day been, work all right?
lines.do: Leans on the counter, rubs his knee, glances at the cupboard and points behind the rice

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ah, behind the rice, brilliant, thank you! Oh no, poor Colin, well, poor you really, being blamed for a bed in a lift! Was it a patient's bed or just a spare one? My day's been fine, honestly, just emails and a spreadsheet that wouldn't behave. I'm glad to be done really. Are you sitting down at all before you cook? Your knee sounds sore.
lines.do: Reaches behind the rice, finds the oats, and starts weighing out flour and butter into a bowl

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, it was a spare one thank god, empty, but still a nightmare, doors wouldn't close and some poor visitor stood there watching us. Yeah I'll sit down in a bit, soon as I've got the onions going, cooking's my sitting down really. Ooh, make it a proper crumble topping, loads of oats, yeah? Do you want a tune on? I was thinking some old Gregory Isaacs while I chop.
lines.do: Pulls onions and a chopping board out, rolls his shoulders, takes a pan from the cupboard

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Oh yes, Gregory Isaacs please, that's perfect cooking music! And don't worry, loads of oats, proper crunchy topping. Do you want me to pass you anything while I'm over here? I'm only rubbing butter into flour, so I can chat all day.
lines.do: Rubs butter into flour with fingertips, glances over at Junior chopping

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, nah you're alright, just stay put with your butter. Actually, one thing, can you stick the Gregory Isaacs on? My phone's by the kettle, just put on the speaker, any of the old stuff. I'm not fussy, he's all good. Ooh and don't judge how many onions I'm doing, it's a big pot!
lines.do: Starts chopping onions, nods toward the phone by the kettle

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Oh, course, I'll do it now! My hands are all butter though, hang on, I'll use my knuckle. Is it by the kettle, this one? Right, Gregory Isaacs, any of the old stuff. Is that loud enough or do you want it up a bit? And honestly, onions are the best bit, the more the better!
lines.do: Wipes fingertips on a tea towel, goes to the phone by the kettle and puts Gregory Isaacs on the speaker, then goes back to the crumble bowl

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Lovely, that's perfect, thanks Hayley! Ooh that's the good stuff. Right, onions are going in, then garlic and the scotch bonnet, one bit only, I promise. Do you do the crumble with cinnamon? Mine always had loads of cinnamon, my mum swore by it.
lines.do: Scrapes the onions into the pan, nods along to the music, tapping the counter

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ooh, I do a bit of cinnamon, yeah, it's lovely with apples. Your mum was right! I'll put a good pinch in the apples and a bit in the topping too. Did she make crumble a lot, then, or was cinnamon in everything?
lines.do: Tips oats into the bowl and mixes them through the butter and flour, then reaches for the cinnamon jar.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, my mum put cinnamon in everything, mate, rice pudding, porridge, she even tried it in a stew once and we never let her forget it. Crumble every Sunday though, with custard, proper thick yellow custard. Ooh that reminds me, have we got any custard powder, or are we doing cream? Right, garlic going in now, smell that!
lines.do: Stirs the onions, adds garlic, then carefully drops in one piece of scotch bonnet, bobbing his head to the music

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ooh, good question, I think there's a tin of custard powder in the cupboard by the fridge, the yellow one? Hang on, I'll have a look. If not, cream's fine, or I could whip up proper custard from scratch, I've got eggs. Oh that smells amazing already, the garlic! Is it a Sunday custard sort of thing, the really thick kind that holds a spoon up?
lines.do: Wipes buttery fingers on the tea towel, opens the cupboard by the fridge and looks for the custard powder

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, yes, the thick kind, proper spoon-standing custard, none of that thin stuff! Yellow tin by the fridge, that's the one. If it's empty don't worry, cream's fine, I'm easy. Oh this is smelling good already, wait till the chicken goes in.
lines.do: Stirs the onions and garlic, sways to the music, then starts cutting up the chicken

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Found it, there's loads left in the tin, enough for a proper thick one. I'll do that instead of cream then, I'll make it up once the crumble's in. Is it just water and a bit of milk, or do you do it the proper way with the sugar and everything? Oh and sit down once the chicken's in, honestly, I'll keep an eye on things if you need a minute!
lines.do: Finds the yellow tin of custard powder, puts it on the counter, then starts peeling and slicing apples for the crumble.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, just water and a splash of milk, mate, with plenty of sugar, that's how my mum did it. You're a star though, honestly. Right, chicken's going in now, then chickpeas, then I'll sit down, promise. Ooh, you hear that bassline? Gregory never misses.
lines.do: Tips the chopped chicken into the pan and stirs, then opens a tin of chickpeas and drains it in the sink

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, he never does! Right, these apples are going in with the cinnamon, then it's in the oven and I'll do the custard after. Is the oven free, by the way, or have you got anything going in it? Oh, and have you sat down yet? Go on, two minutes!
lines.do: Slices the last apple into a bowl, sprinkles cinnamon and sugar over it, and tosses it with her fingers, bobbing along to the music.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Oven's free, yeah, all yours, I've only got the hob going. Ha, alright alright, I'm sitting, look! Just letting the chickpeas go in first, then it's a lid on and a simmer for an hour or so. Ooh, that's my knee thanking you already.
lines.do: Tips chickpeas into the pan, stirs, puts the lid on and lowers the heat, then pulls a chair out and sits with a sigh

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Good, that's better! Right, crumble topping on, and then it's in the oven. Twenty-five minutes or so, I think, then I'll do the custard nearer the time so it's hot. Oh, did you ever hear back about your rota, or is it just this weekend as normal?
lines.do: Spoons the apples into a dish, scatters the crumble topping over, and slides it into the oven.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Rota? Ha, yeah just this weekend as normal, Sat and Sun, seven till seven. Be glad when it's done though, my back's already moaning about it. Oh, I keep meaning to top up the electric, hang on, let me do that on my phone before I forget again. Then I'll wash my stuff up, promise.
lines.do: Gets up slowly from the chair, picks up phone from by the kettle, taps at it to top up the electric

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ooh, good, sort that before you forget! Don't worry about the washing up, honestly, I'll give you a hand in a bit once I've sorted my bowls. Is it one of those top-ups that takes ages to go through? Ours always sulks.
lines.do: Starts rinsing her mixing bowl in the sink, humming along to the music

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, it's going through, slow as anything, ours sulks too. There, done, the electric's sorted, no more panic at midnight. Right, now my washing up, and don't you dare help, you've done the crumble. Ooh, hear that? This one's my favourite Gregory.
lines.do: Puts phone down by the kettle, runs hot water into the sink and starts washing his mug and bowl, nodding to the music.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, I wasn't going to! I'm just rinsing this bowl and then I'll wipe down the side. Oh, is that the one with the bassline? Lovely. Do you want a cuppa while you're stood there, since the kettle's right by you?
lines.do: Rinses the mixing bowl, stacks it on the rack, and wipes the worktop with a cloth, bobbing along to the music.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Go on then, a cuppa would be lovely, ta Hayley, milk no sugar. Ooh, my mug's still soapy, use the blue one, that's clean. Right, nearly done here, then I'm putting my feet up till that crumble comes out!
lines.do: Rinses his bowl and stacks it on the rack, wipes his hands on his trousers, nodding to the music.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Course, milk no sugar, blue one, got it! Sit yourself down and I'll bring it over. Oh, and the crumble's got about twenty minutes yet, so no rush at all.
lines.do: Fills the kettle and switches it on, takes the blue mug from the cupboard and drops a teabag in.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Cheers Hayley, you're a gem. Ooh, I'll sit with it and stir the stew in a bit. Here, what are you doing tomorrow, anything nice? I'll be stuck wheeling people about all day, ha.
lines.do: Dries hands on a tea towel and lowers himself back into the chair, rubbing his knee.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Here you go, one blue mug, milk no sugar! Ooh, tomorrow, not much, honestly. I might have a lazy morning, then pop to the charity shops if it's not too cold, my chest doesn't love the damp. Then probably a long phone call with my sister, she'll talk for an hour! Are you getting a proper break at all, or is it straight through?
lines.do: Makes the tea, carries the blue mug over and sets it down by Junior.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ah cheers Hayley, lovely. Break? Ha, half an hour if I'm lucky, and that's if nobody's bleep goes off the second I open my sandwich. Colin usually covers me for ten minutes though, he's alright. Charity shops, ooh, keep an eye out for records, yeah? Any old soul or reggae, I'll give you a few quid for anything decent. Proper bargains in them boxes sometimes.
lines.do: Picks up the blue mug, takes a sip, and stretches his legs out under the table.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Records, oh go on, I'll have a proper rummage! Soul and reggae, got it. I'll text you if I find anything so you're not guessing. Right, I'll stick the custard on in a bit. Is your stew alright to leave a minute, or does it want a stir?
lines.do: Leans against the counter, glances at the oven timer, then fishes in her cardigan pocket for her inhaler and puts it on the side.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ooh, it's alright for a bit, mate, it's on a low simmer. Actually go on, I'll give it a quick stir anyway, I can't help myself. Here, you alright for your chest in this kitchen, with the steam and that? Open the window a crack if you want, I won't mind.
lines.do: Gets up with a small groan, lifts the lid, stirs the stew and sniffs it, then puts the lid back on.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Oh, I'm alright, honestly, it's only a bit of steam. I'll crack the window just a tiny bit though, thanks! Smells gorgeous, by the way. Is that the scotch bonnet I can smell, or am I imagining it? Ha, I'm already bracing myself.
lines.do: Opens the kitchen window a crack, then checks the oven light and puts the custard powder and a saucepan out on the hob.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, you're not imagining it, that's the scotch bonnet saying hello! Only the one though, I swear. Honestly you'll be fine, it's more flavour than fire. Here, if it's too much I've got yoghurt in the fridge, a spoon of that sorts it right out. Ooh, I should put some rice on in a bit as well, you want rice or bread with yours?
lines.do: Sips tea, leans back in the chair and nods toward the pan

lines.do: Takes the crumble out of the oven and sets it on the hob to cool, then leans on the counter near Junior.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, yes, scotch bonnet, but only the one and I left it whole, so you get the flavour without the fire, mostly! I'm not saying I won't fish it out if your eyes start watering though. Bowls would be brilliant, yeah, they're in the cupboard on the left, the big ones, not those little saucer things Yousif likes. Oh and that crumble looks lovely, what's in it, just apple? My knees are killing me so I'm not moving far, ha.
lines.do: Stirs the pot, tastes from the wooden spoon, nods at the cupboard

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Just apple, but I've thrown some cinnamon and a bit of oat in the topping, so it's a bit crunchy! Oh your poor knees, sit tight, I'll sort it. Big ones on the left, got it. How many do you want, just the two of us, or will Yousif come and grab one?
lines.do: Opens the left cupboard and takes down two big bowls, then looks for spoons in the drawer.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Just the two of us for now, but get a third one out anyway, Yousif'll turn up the second he smells it, he always does, ha. I've texted him. Spoons are in the drawer under, no, the one next to it, yeah that one. Oh, and you're a star, my knees thank you.
lines.do: Stirs the pot and turns the heat down a little, nods at the drawer

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Got it, three bowls, and spoons. Right, here you go, sit down if you like, I'll bring it over. Do you want rice or anything with it, or is it just the stew? And how were your knees today, was it the walk home or have they been bad all week?
lines.do: Sets three bowls and spoons on the counter beside the pot, then fetches the crumble closer.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ah no rice, I never got round to it, just the stew is fine, there's dumplings in it anyway so it's proper filling, ha. And the knees, honestly it's the whole week, all that standing and pushing beds up and down corridors, then the walk home finished them off. Right, I'm sitting, I'm sitting. Ooh, give us a taste of that crumble edge while you're there, just the crunchy bit!
lines.do: Turns the heat off under the pot and lowers himself onto a kitchen chair, rubbing one knee.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, go on then, but just the crunchy bit, it's still piping hot underneath! Here, careful. Right, stew coming over, I'll dish it up. Do you want me to bring you a glass of water too, in case the scotch bonnet gets you? Not that it'll get you, you're the one who made it, ha!
lines.do: Breaks off a crunchy bit of topping with a spoon and hands it to Junior, then ladles stew into two bowls.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Mm, that's good, proper crunchy! Yeah water please, ha, though I'm not worried, I went easy. Thanks Hayley, honestly. Right, give it a minute to cool and tell me what you've been up to today, was it a dead day at work or did you get loads done? Oh, and Yousif still hasn't answered me, I might give him a shout.
lines.do: Chews the crumble topping, nods, rubs his knee again

lines.name: Yousif Al-Ani
lines.say: coming. two minutes
lines.do: Pauses the film essay, puts the sketchbook down, and goes through to the kitchen to get a bowl of stew.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Oh hiya Yousif! Perfect timing, there's a bowl here with your name on it. Junior's done dumplings and everything, and there's crumble after if you fancy it. Do you want water with yours, or are you a brave one with the scotch bonnet? Sorry, let me just grab Junior's water first, ha.
lines.do: Pours a glass of water from the tap and puts it in front of Junior, then slides a bowl of stew towards Yousif.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ah there he is! Told you, Hayley, smell of it and he's here, ha. Sit down, Yousif, grab the bowl. Dumplings are in there, go easy on the scotch bonnet if you find it, it's the one whole pepper floating about. Water's a good shout, yeah. So what you been working on today, mate, still that logo thing?
lines.do: Waves a spoon at the empty chair and takes a first mouthful of stew, blowing on it.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Here, sit down, Yousif, I'll bring yours over. Don't mind me, I'm just getting my own. Junior's been on his feet all week, so he's earned the sit. Oh, and how's the logo going, by the way? Sorry, Junior asked first, ha, I'll shush and let you answer.
lines.do: Carries the third bowl of stew to the table, then ladles her own and sits down with it.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Oi Hayley, you didn't say what you got up to today, don't think I've forgotten, ha. Go on Yousif, how's the logo? And tell me the stew's not too salty, I never know with the dumplings.
lines.do: Takes a sip of water, picks up his spoon and digs into the stew, looking between them.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, fair, I've been dodging! Honestly just emails and a mountain of spreadsheets today, nothing exciting. Right, I'm trying this stew now. Oh that's lovely, Junior, not too salty at all, the dumplings are spot on. And the scotch bonnet's just a nice warmth, I'm still alive, ha.
lines.do: Takes a mouthful of stew, nods happily, and reaches for her water.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ah good, not too salty, that's a weight off, ha. Yousif, you're quiet, mate, is it alright? Tell me honestly, I can take it. And Hayley, spreadsheets, ugh, you deserve double crumble for that. After this I'm putting a record on if anyone wants, Gregory Isaacs or some old Motown, your pick.
lines.do: Tears a dumpling in half with his spoon and grins across the table.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ooh, Motown please, Junior, anything but me picking, I'll only dither! Yousif, you alright? You've gone quiet, is the stew too hot for you? I can fetch you some water if so, honestly it's no bother.
lines.do: Takes another spoonful of stew and glances over at Yousif.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Yousif, mate, you've gone proper quiet, ha. If it's too hot just say, there's bread somewhere, I think. Right, I'm doing the record after this. Motown it is, Hayley, I'll find the Four Tops. Go on Yousif, how's the logo?
lines.do: Takes another mouthful of stew and points his spoon towards the living room.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, maybe he's just hungry and can't talk with his mouth full! Leave him, Junior, let him eat. Oh, and while we're all sat here, I was thinking about doing a flat meal before Christmas, nothing fancy. Yousif, I know you said no earlier, so no pressure, honestly!
lines.do: Eats a spoonful of stew and smiles at Yousif.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ooh a flat meal, yeah I'm in, Hayley! Count me in, I'll do a big pot of something, jerk chicken maybe, or the stew again, ha. Yousif, no pressure mate, but you'd get fed and I'd be less loud if you came. Right, and I'm doing that Four Tops after this, who's on washing up? Not me, I've done the cooking, ha, joking, I'll do my pot.
lines.do: Grins, mops the bowl with a bit of dumpling, and rubs his knee again.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, I'll do the washing up, honestly, you've both earned a sit. Cooking's the fun bit, I don't mind the sink. Yousif, how's the stew, is it alright? And Junior, jerk chicken, yes please, I'll make a pudding. Sorry, I'm rambling, eat!
lines.do: Takes another spoonful of stew and smiles at them both.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Right, Four Tops it is then, I'll sort it once I've finished this. Hayley, you don't have to do the lot though, I'll dry up at least, my knees can cope with standing at a sink, ha. Yousif, no stress mate, eat your stew.
lines.do: Finishes the last of his stew and scrapes the bowl, then glances toward the living room.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, deal, you dry and I'll wash, and no arguing! Let me just finish this bit of stew first, it's too good to leave. Yousif, there's crumble whenever you want it, no rush. Oh and Junior, put the Four Tops on low-ish, yeah? Not for me, ha, just so the neighbours don't complain!
lines.do: Takes another spoonful of stew, smiling at them both.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Low-ish, yeah, Hayley, I'm not a animal, ha. Right, you wash, I dry, deal. Yousif, leave your bowl when you're done, mate, and there's crumble waiting. I'll go find the Four Tops.
lines.do: Stands up with a small wince, picks up his bowl and heads toward the living room to the record player.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Right, I'll get the crumble out for you, Yousif, if you want it. There's custard in the fridge, or cream, whichever. Honestly no rush, I'll start on the pots once I've finished this.
lines.do: Finishes the last of her stew and gets up to take the crumble from the counter.

lines.name: Yousif Al-Ani
lines.say: stew is good. not too salty. logo is done, waiting for helen. i will have the crumble, thanks.
lines.do: Sits down, eats the stew, nods at Hayley when she brings the crumble.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Glad it's not too salty, Yousif! Ooh, logo's done, that's good, hope Helen likes it. Custard or cream on yours? I'll just stick the kettle on after, anyone want a tea?
lines.do: Puts the crumble bowl in front of Yousif, then fetches the custard from the fridge.

lines.name: Yousif Al-Ani
lines.say: cream, thanks. no tea for me. i will wash my bowl after.
lines.do: Eats the crumble slowly.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: No tea for you, fair enough! Right, I'll stick the kettle on for me anyway, and then I'll make a start on the pots. Just leave your bowl, Yousif, honestly, I'll do it.
lines.do: Fills the kettle, switches it on, and starts stacking the empty bowls by the sink.

lines.name: Yousif Al-Ani
lines.say: thanks for the crumble. it is good.
lines.do: Finishes the crumble, takes his bowl to the sink, rinses it quickly and leaves it on the rack.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Oh I love this one! Who is it, is it Al Green? My nan used to have this on when she did the ironing. Is that seconds of stew still going, or have I got to be good? Go on, tiny bowl, I'll say it's for the crumble's sake.
lines.do: Sits down on the sofa, tucking her feet up, and glances at the records on the floor.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Al Green, yes! Your nan had taste. Go on, it's a tiny bowl, I won't tell the crumble. Actually it's apple pudding, innit, don't let me get it wrong. Sit tight, I'll fetch it, there's plenty. You want bread with it? I got a proper crusty one from the market, two quid, bargain.
lines.do: Heads to the kitchen to ladle a small bowl of stew, turns the record down a little first

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Yes please, bread too, go on, you've twisted my arm! Ooh, and this is such a good record, my mum would've known every word of it. Do you know, I keep thinking we should do a proper flat meal before Christmas, everyone round the table. Would you be up for that, do you think?
lines.do: Settles back into the sofa, humming along to the record.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Oh yes, I'm up for that, definitely! I'll do the stew again, or jerk chicken, ooh, or we all do a dish each, that'd be good. Not this weekend though, I'm on both days, seven till seven. Week after? And we get Yousif out of his room for it, he'll say he's got a deadline, he always says that. Here, bread, and mind, it's hot.
lines.do: Brings the bowl of stew and a chunk of bread through and hands it to Hayley, then sits on the arm of the armchair

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ooh, this smells amazing, thank you! Week after sounds perfect, honestly. I'll make a pudding, maybe another crumble, or is that too much crumble? Ha. And yes, Yousif, we'll prise him out, I'll bribe him with food. Do you want to put the next record on after this one, or have you got a plan for the order?
lines.do: Takes the bowl and bread, blows on the stew, and tears off a bit of bread.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, plan? No plan, I go by feel. Right, next one's gotta be Delroy Wilson or a bit of Gregory Isaacs, slow it down a bit. Or Bill Withers, your nan would've liked him too. Hold on, my knees, let me just get down to the box. Eat your stew while it's hot, don't wait on me!
lines.do: Slides off the armchair arm with a small wince, crouches by the records on the floor and flips through them

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ooh, Bill Withers, yes! Lean on Me, or Ain't No Sunshine, my mum would've sung the whole thing. Mind your knees though, do you want me to come and flip through? No, honestly, I'll stay put, this stew's too good. Oh, it's got a proper kick, hasn't it? In a good way, I'm just going to need a glass of water in a minute, ha.
lines.do: Eats a spoonful of stew, fans her mouth, laughing, and keeps her feet tucked up on the sofa.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, told you, proper kick! Jerk seasoning, I got a bit heavy handed with it. Water's in the fridge, help yourself. Right, found it, Bill Withers, Just As I Am, the one with Ain't No Sunshine on. Oh, and listen, you know what, this is the first night I've sat down properly all week.
lines.do: Pulls the record from the box, slides it out of the sleeve, and puts it on the turntable, then eases himself back into the armchair.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Aw, is it? You've earned it, honestly. Twelve-hour shifts on your feet, and then you cook for everyone as well! Are you all right for the weekend, though? Do you get a proper break at work, or is it just grabbing a sandwich when you can?
lines.do: Eats another spoonful of stew, then dips the bread in it and settles back as the record starts.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, break? Supposed to get half an hour, but it's whenever the bleep lets you. Yesterday I had a cheese sandwich in the lift, honest. Colin saves me a seat sometimes if he's about. But I'm all right, you get used to it, it's just the knees that complain. Anyway, enough of me, how's your day been, you got much done working from home or did the telly win?
lines.do: Settles back in the armchair, rubs one knee, listens to the record

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ha, the telly did not win, honestly! I got loads done, I did that whole report thing for Dan and then I had a go at the mouldy bit in the bathroom, well, messaged the agent about it anyway. Fingers crossed they reply. Cheese sandwich in a lift though, that's tragic! Do you want me to make you something to take in tomorrow? I could do a flapjack or something, it's no bother.
lines.do: Dips the last of the bread in the stew, smiling, and nods along to the record.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Aw, flapjack, you're a star, yes please, if it's no bother! I'd eat it in the lift and think of you. Oh, and the mould, ugh, the agent takes forever, I'll chase them Monday if they don't answer, I've got their number somewhere. Right, hang on, this is the bit coming up, listen to that bassline.
lines.do: Sits forward in the armchair, taps the beat on his knee, grinning

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ooh, that bassline! Oh, that's gorgeous. Thanks for saying you'll chase the agent, Junior, honestly, that's a weight off. I'll do the flapjack first thing in the morning so it's fresh, before you head off. Is seven still when you leave? I'll set an alarm, I don't mind.
lines.do: Taps her foot along to the bassline, scrapes the last of the stew from the bowl and sets it on the floor by the sofa.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, quarter to seven, yeah, but don't set an alarm for me, Hayley, I'll be bleary enough as it is. Leave it on the side if you've done it, I'll grab it on the way out. Honestly though, you're too good to me. Right, you want your water? I'll get it, my knees need the walk anyway.
lines.do: Gets up from the armchair with a small groan and heads to the kitchen for water, humming along to the record

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Ah, you're a star, thank you! Go on, I'll keep your seat warm. Honestly though, I'll just do the flapjack tonight instead, then it's done and you can grab it whenever. Is oats and golden syrup all right, or are you a raisin person?
lines.do: Stretches her legs out on the sofa, smiling, and turns toward the kitchen as Junior goes.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Oats and golden syrup, definitely, no raisins, raisins are a crime in a flapjack, ha. Hayley, you don't have to do it tonight though, honest, it's gone ten! But if you're doing it I won't stop you. Here, water.
lines.do: Fills a glass of water at the kitchen tap, then carries it back through to the living room and hands it over.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Oh thank you, lovely. Ha, you're right, it's gone ten, I'm being daft. Tell you what, I'll do it in the morning after all, I'll be up anyway. Quarter to seven, you said? I'll leave it on the side. Now sit down, this is the best bit of the record, isn't it?
lines.do: Takes the glass, sips the water, and settles back into the sofa.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Ha, go on then, I'm sat. Oh that's lovely, that is. Hayley, I'm gonna have to call it soon though, seven o'clock start, my knees are already moaning at me. One more track and then I'll be heading to bed, yeah? Thanks for tonight, honest, it was a good one.
lines.do: Sinks back into the armchair, nodding along to the bassline.

lines.name: Hayley Johnson
lines.say: Course you should, go on, get to bed! Thanks for tonight, Junior, honestly, that was lovely. Good luck tomorrow, and I'll leave the flapjack on the side for you. Night!
lines.do: Sips her water, smiles and waves as he heads off, then stays on the sofa to finish the track.

lines.name: Junior Edwards
lines.say: Night Hayley, thanks for the company, and the flapjack! Don't stay up too late with the telly, ha.
lines.do: Lifts the needle gently after the track, slides the record into its sleeve, picks up his bowl and heads off to his room.
